Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Which statement is a normative statement?

options.A: Aggregate demand will increase following a decrease in interest rates.
options.B: A rise in unemployment will decrease inflationary pressures.
options.C: The incentive to work will rise if benefit payments are reduced.
options.D: Unsustainable economic growth is more harmful to the economy than hyperinflation.

questions.questionText: Which combination best describes the basic economic problem? resources wants

options.A: limited limited
options.B: limited unlimited
options.C: unlimited limited
options.D: unlimited unlimited

questions.questionText: What is the main reason an economy is unlikely to rely completely on market forces to allocate resources?

options.A: Demerit goods will be over supplied.
options.B: Merit goods will be under supplied.
options.C: Private goods will not be supplied.
options.D: Public goods will not be supplied.

questions.questionText: What is the opportunity cost to a person of spending $20 on a new pair of sports shoes?

options.A: all the other things the person could have bought
options.B: the cost of getting to the sports shop
options.C: the current value of the person’s old pair of shoes
options.D: the next best thing that could have been bought with the $20

questions.questionText: What is the definition of effective demand?

options.A: demand that is speculative
options.B: demand that is supported by the ability to pay
options.C: the relationship between price and quantity demanded
options.D: the total amount demanded by consumers

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for good X is –2.4, its income elasticity of demand is –0.4 and the cross elasticity of demand for good X with respect to good Y is +0.8. What is the correct description of good X?

options.A: inferior good, price-elastic demand and substitute for good Y
options.B: inferior good, price-inelastic demand and complement to good Y
options.C: normal good, price-elastic demand and complement to good Y
options.D: normal good, price-inelastic demand and substitute for good Y

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two straight line demand curves, X and Y. price X Y O quantity What is correct about curves X and Y?

options.A: Both X and Y are unit price elastic over their whole length.
options.B: Both X and Y have the same elasticity at every price.
options.C: X has a higher price elasticity than Y at every price.
options.D: Y is more likely to have substitutes than X.

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of the supply of yoghurt is estimated to be +1.5. If the demand for yoghurt rises and price rises by 20%, how much more will be supplied to the market?

Butter is a normal good. It is in joint demand with bread and in joint supply with buttermilk. The demand for butter increases because of a rise in consumer incomes. What are the effects of this increase on the prices of bread and buttermilk? price of price of bread buttermilk

options.A: decreases decreases
options.B: decreases increases
options.C: increases decreases
options.D: increases increases

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a competitive market in equilibrium with price P and quantity Q sold. V S price P W U D O Q quantity Which area represents the producer surplus?

options.A: PWU B PVW C OUWQ D OPWQ

questions.questionText: A policy that aims to reduce the degree of inequality of income will also reduce the level of employment in a country. What is most likely to be such a policy?

options.A: The effective minimum wage is increased by 25%.
options.B: The rate of income tax paid by the lowest band of earners is reduced.
options.C: The government increases the level of subsidies given to producers of some merit goods.
options.D: The government provides more goods that are regarded as essential.

questions.questionText: What explains the underconsumption of merit goods?

options.A: Their value is not fully understood by consumers.
options.B: They are unproductive goods and services.
options.C: They can only be provided by the government.
options.D: They are only provided by private sector businesses.

questions.questionText: A country uses an income tax under which the first $10000 of income is tax-free, the next $20000 is taxed at 20% and any income over $30000 is taxed at a top rate of 40%. It also levies a sales tax of 10% on most products. Which combination of tax changes is most likely to create a more equal distribution of income in the country? income tax sales tax

options.A: a higher tax-free allowance a higher rate of tax
options.B: a higher top rate of tax a lower rate of tax
options.C: a lower tax-free allowance a higher number of exempt goods
options.D: a lower top rate of tax a lower number of exempt goods

questions.questionText: The table shows real GDP expressed as an index number in each quarter of 2021. index of GDP 2021 in real terms (2020 = 100) Q1 99.4 Q2 99.3 Q3 100.1 Q4 100.4 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Inflation reduced the real value of GDP in the first six months of 2021.
options.B: Real GDP was lower at the end of 2021 than 2020.
options.C: The economy was in recession at the end of the first six months of 2021.
options.D: The standard of living was higher at the end of 2021 than in 2020.

questions.questionText: What is least likely to cause a simultaneous increase in demand-pull and cost-push inflation?

options.A: depreciation of currency
options.B: increased import tariffs
options.C: decreased spending on infrastructure
options.D: increased wages

questions.questionText: According to the circular flow of income, what would be the immediate result of an increase in the value of a country’s exports?

options.A: imports would increase
options.B: national income would increase
options.C: savings would increase
options.D: taxes would increase

questions.questionText: To calculate the unemployment rate, the number unemployed is related to

options.A: the total adult population aged 18–65.
options.B: the number of unemployed who are seeking work.
options.C: the total number in full-time employment.
options.D: the total population in the labour force.

questions.questionText: Aggregate demand in an economy may decrease as a result of an increase in

options.A: consumption expenditure.
options.B: government expenditure.
options.C: import expenditure.
options.D: investment expenditure.

questions.questionText: A government has a balanced budget. It decides to increase its spending by 10%. Which increase in government revenue would produce a budget surplus?

An economy has an unemployment rate of 8%, an increase of 2% from the previous year. At the same time, the current account deficit rose from 3% of GDP to 4% of GDP. What would be most likely to reduce both unemployment and the current account deficit?

options.A: decrease government spending
options.B: depreciation of the currency
options.C: increase indirect taxation
options.D: increase interest rates

questions.questionText: The diagram shows aggregate demand (AD) curves for an economy. price level AD AD O real output Which combination is most likely to have caused the shift from AD to AD ?
What can be considered an expansionary supply-side policy?

options.A: an increase in government expenditure on training
options.B: an increase in sales tax
options.C: an increase in the rate of interest
options.D: an increase of the exchange rate

questions.questionText: The table indicates the factor inputs required to produce wheat and cars in countries X and Y. units of factor units of factor inputs to produce inputs to produce one tonne of wheat one car country X 4 2 country Y 8 6 What makes it possible for both countries to benefit from trade?

options.A: Country X has an absolute advantage in wheat and car production.
options.B: Country Y has an absolute advantage in wheat and car production.
options.C: Country Y has a comparative advantage in wheat production.
options.D: Opportunity cost of wheat and car production is the same between countries.

questions.questionText: A government decides to allow the country’s currency to depreciate to remove the deficit on its current account of the balance of payments. What is the most likely reason why this would not work?

options.A: The country gains a competitive advantage from the depreciation.
options.B: The country has a surplus on its capital and financial accounts.
options.C: The price elasticities of demand for the country’s exports and imports are greater than one.
options.D: There are high trade barriers with the country’s main trading partners.

questions.questionText: When must the terms of trade of a country change?

options.A: when the volume of exports falls and the volume of imports rises
options.B: when the total value of exports falls and the total value of imports rises
options.C: when the balance of trade in goods moves from deficit to surplus
options.D: when the average price of exports rises and the average price of imports falls

questions.questionText: The table shows an extract from a country’s balance of payments. exports imports $ billion $ billion trade in goods 150 200 trade in services 70 50 primary (investment) income 120 100 secondary (transfer) income 15 20 What is the current account balance?

options.A: –$10bn B –$15bn C –$30bn D –$50bn
